utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Good morning, Mr. Witness. Mr. Karadzic, please continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Excellency. Good morning to all. Good morning, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As you remember, yesterday we established that the bullet travelled vertically from bottom up. Did you establish what the situation was on the horizontal plane in relation to a perpendicular line? How did the bullet travel in relation to the walls of the room? Was it under a 90-degree angle or did it go left to right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly, so that is to say that without my own report, I cannot say. After all, it's been 15 or 16 years. My report should say what I did and which measures were reported.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The Prosecution was kind enough to provide us with the entire report, including your own. Can I offer you a paper copy so that you see what it was you did and what you recorded?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please take a minute or two to have a look at it and see what was actually done.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. I think that this may be in 65 ter 10397. The Prosecutor notified us of that this morning, and it may be that we can all look at that on the e-court, if I'm correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Let's up-load that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: If that might not be broadcast as well. Now, I don't believe we have an English translation of this witness's report. We just have the B/C/S original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I think the witness has read his report.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What we have on our screens is an official report. However, under that 65 ter number, on the further pages we should see the crime technician's report. Can we sort of leaf through this? Can we see the next pages? Can you go one page further?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, is this your part of the report? Yes, it is. Crime technician's report. Right. It is not being broadcast.

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the first page of my report, where we see the date, the crime committed, the location, the subject of the attack, and then a description showing that everything was described and photographed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please confirm, then, that a 7.62-millimetre bullet flew through the foil at 116 centimetres, then the curtain at 116.5 centimetres, hit the person concerned in the chest, and then hit a wardrobe at a height of 124 centimetres, flew through the wardrobe, and exited at 131 centimetres, so it travelled according to a vertical line. Let us see whether there was any horizontal change. Next page, please.

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the second page of my report. That is where the traces found are recorded. So we see that it was the vertical plane that was dealt with, not the horizontal.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Don't you think that the horizontal plane is also very important in order to establish where the bullet had come from?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not working on this investigation on my own. Zdenko Eterovic, an investigating judge of the Higher Court in Sarajevo, was in charge of this investigation, so he's the person who asked what was supposed to be done. My report contains all the measures I took at the request of the investigating judge who was in charge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. I am not trying to establish whose omission it was, but let us just look further through this. Can we see what the angle of descent of that bullet was?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apart from the report, there was compiled by the inspector, listed under number 2, and also if you look at my report and my photo file, which cannot be seen properly, there is also a death certificate issued by the Dobrinja Hospital. We have a statement as well. I think it's a statement that was taken by a member of the Security Services, or, rather, the police station in Novi Grad, and also a crime report that was signed by the head of the centre. So there are no expert findings, apart from what I did at the request of the investigating judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You do agree that the lines were very close there and that they even split the building in two, as it were?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the measurements I have, that is within the apartment, and it has to do with the entry of the bullet into the apartment and everything that happened in that room. So the window was on one side, and the bullet happened to be on the opposite wall at a height of - what was it? - 132 centimetres. It is only when we look through the window that we could see from where this could have been fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So what you did then was draw the conclusion that somebody had fired from the Serb positions in the Street of Miroslava Krleze; it was either you or somebody from your team that came to this conclusion. It says "from Dobrinja 1"; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am looking at the photo file now, and it is not legible because it's a photocopy. It says "Photo 10."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter's note: It is too fast for interpreting everything the witness is reading.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, probably you spoke a bit too fast, and the interpreters had difficulty following you. Did you say anything about photo 10? Shall we see page 11, then. And we can collapse the English part because we don't have an English translation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a photograph that is part of my entire photo documentation. This is the view from the window of the apartment where the incident had occurred. Buildings can be seen in the background, and there is a caption underneath saying that an arrow marks the building in Dobrinja number 1 that is under aggressor occupation from which the bullet most probably arrived. Now, what does "most probably" mean? The bullet might have arrived from these positions. However, as I've already said, I'm a crime technician, and in this case I was authorised by the investigating judge to carry out the measurements and to use a string. Now, is this relevant before a court of law? That was not my decision. The investigating judge was pleased with what we had did. And after carrying out the measures and taking the photographs, we left the scene. Now, whether somebody came subsequently, that I do not know. What else can I say? It says here an arrow marks the building, et cetera. As you can see here on the screen yourselves, we do not have a colour photograph, so you can barely discern anything. You can just see certain contours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I, or do you have anything else, Your Excellency?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So now you're taking a photograph of a building that is on the Serb side, and you mark that building as the most probable source of fire, as you say. So there are these two planes here, the horizontal and the vertical. We see that the bullet is rising, ascending, and the ascent is rather sharp. How big is this room?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you take into account that this is an averaged-sized room in Dobrinja, the maximum width can be between four or five metres maximum. As for the vertical from 116 to 132, let's say it was 16 centimetres. That was the difference, in terms of height.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So the fire came from a lower area, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's hard to say from this point of view. However, at the site, itself, this could be shown very simply. Again, if these points were to be found at 132 and 116, and that line, that trajectory, would show what the direction was. For example, if the firing had come from the entrance into the building, perhaps the bullet could have entered at 116 centimetres, but it probably would have stopped on the ceiling. So I think that this vertical height corresponds to this trajectory; namely, that it had been fired from that distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How far away is the building that you marked as the source of fire?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is hard to say now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What is the angle? What is the angle in relation to the horizontal plane, the floor? It ascends 16 centimetres?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not in a position to say that. I didn't do it there and then. I wasn't asked to do it. The calculations can be done later. For example, if we take 116 down to zero, and then you can calculate what the angle is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, don't you think that we should have two angles, the horizontal and the vertical angle, so that we could mark this building, and that we should also have the size of the room, itself, in order to be able to calculate the angle and to have the distance between this building and the other building?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that there is one angle there. If the entry was at 116 and if it ends at 132, then we can say that there is a triangle there, and then the line can be calculated. But this is mathematics that I cannot go into now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, the depth of the room is of crucial importance for that angle. How far in depth does the room go? It's not the same if it's three or five metres, is it? And, secondly, did you see what the situation was in relation to the horizontal plane to see what the building was? Was it 90 degrees?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you just now, and my report says what I did. I keep repeating that I did not work in relation to the horizontal plane. At the request of the Prosecutor -- no, not the request of the Prosecutor. He is now a prosecutor who was in charge of investigations, but at that time it was the investigating judge. He asked me to do what I was supposed to do, and that's what I did at his request. We specifically state the address where this happened, which apartment it is. Nothing has changed there. So as far as the width of that room is concerned, that can be established. However, I repeat, once again, I did not take the measurements, and they are not contained in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You stand by that; namely, that this happened on the fourth floor in the Street of Dzavaharlala Nehrua number 10; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My report says "J Nehru 10/4 on the 14th of May, 1995, at 2345 hours." I believe that the same is written in the official reports of my colleagues and the investigating judge, who were all on the scene. Let me say one more thing. I am not a person who is in charge of the team that goes to the site. It is the operative from the Security Centre who is in charge of that. That is the person mentioned under number 3. He has a very good knowledge of the area, and he took us to the site when the entire team was brought together.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We are now interested in what you were doing; that is to say, the measurements. Was a sketch made?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can see in my report, no sketch was made, because I was not asked to do that. Only photographs were taken, and a crime technician's report was compiled.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would I be right in saying that I saw in your report that the room was dark, it was 15 to 12 and the room was not lit?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to read that. It says the blinds were down on the window. There was a foil and blinds were down, so the room was dark. According to the report, the room was dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that the shooter could not see inside the room?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said it was dark. Whether he was shooting at random or he had a way of seeing inside, I don't know. But the room was dark and the blinds were down. It's recorded in my report. And the blinds were down still during the investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we try to find out where you were taken? In an earlier incident, the event happened in one street and the on-site investigation in another. Let's see if it happened here as well. The incident happened in Cvitkovica Street, and the on-site investigation was in Dzemal Bijedic Street.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see 1D03066. May I draw everyone's attention to the source. This is a map of Sarajevo. Navigator Sarajevo is an official web site.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Hamdije Kapidzica, former name in brackets, "Dzavaharlal Nehru," do you see that the street, Hamdije Kapidzica Street, is here?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that, and I see the former name in the brackets.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In number 10 of that street, that incident happened, and yesterday you marked lower down -- never mind, we'll look at that later. Could you now mark more precisely where the incident happened?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a very simplified map, but I accept that the incident happened at 10/4 Nehru Street in the apartment where Jasmina Tabakovic was found. It's difficult now to go back to what we discussed yesterday to find out what I marked. We have maps, however, we have old names and new names of streets. Whatever the map says, I agree it was in Nehru Street. After all the on-site investigations I conducted, in various incidents, including burglaries, et cetera, I maybe marked it wrong the last time, but there is no question that it happened in Nehru Street number 10, in that apartment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Why don't we show the witness the map he marked, Exhibit D893, dividing the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, on a split screen. That's what I meant. That's the same. On the other side of the screen, we need yesterday's document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's on its way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that Miroslava Krleze Street was 297?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. That was the street that I marked with number 1. I know that street, and I have friends in that street still today, so I know where the building is. But yesterday I was marking with number 2 Nehru Street, but I wasn't sure. That's what maps are for. We can see here exactly where Nehru Street is. But I stand by my statement, and I'm reading my own report for the first time after many years, and I see that it was in Nehru Street, 10/4. We can now see where the street is, and that's where the apartment is where the incident happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So the incident happened not where you marked yesterday. Could you now use the red pen to mark the building in Hamdije Kapidzica Street where the incident really happened?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this map, I'm not in a position to mark the building accurately. You cannot see that building here. You can only see that it's Hamdije Kapidzica Street, but you can't see any buildings. It's very difficult to show that here. I can only show the Hamdije Kapidzica Street, which on this map is Nehru Street. But where exactly the building was, it's difficult to mark now. I can only mark the street with its new name.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, where do you suggest the marking should be made; on yesterday's map?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's up to you, but, yes, why not. On the right map, if you can mark the area where the Hamdije Kapidzica Street is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: May I ask you to use the red pen to mark "3" and put a circle around it for the place where you think the incident happened?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly now, but I can mark the whole length of Hamdije Kapidzica Street, as designated here [marks]. And we can later establish where number 10 in Nehru Street was. We see that this is Hamdije Kapidzica Street. That's where the building was, and the street was formerly called the Nehru Street, and that's where, at number 10, the incident happened, on the fourth floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How was the apartment oriented? Which side did it face?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's difficult to say after all this time. But photograph 10 could tell us that exactly, because from the window of that room, you see some buildings, and I believe it faced Vojkovici. It faced the number 1 that I marked yesterday, Miroslava Krleze Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I believe in one of your reports, it says the building and the apartment faced south-east and it made an angle of 90 degrees with the south-west line.

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see that in my report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In the meantime, we'll keep this image, as it is, as a separate Defence exhibit. Is it Exhibit D895?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that will be Exhibit D971. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Should he also mark the left photograph, the "KDZ" and date?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It will be kept altogether, as it shows in the current monitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you now agree, Witness, that with number 2, you had marked the street with the number 463, which used to be Zikica Jovanovic Spanac Street, and now it is called Vahida Maglajlic?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what the map says, I agree. But I keep telling you that I was in Nehru Street, and the map can show where you that street was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that these two streets that you marked yesterday are parallel, and the transverse line across them would make an angle of 90 degrees, whereas Hamdije Kapidzica forms an angle with Miroslava Krleze Street?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we get a certain angle between these two streets. They were not perpendicular.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So all these things being what they are, the horizontal plane and the horizontal inclination are decisive in determining where the bullet came from?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the moment when we were doing that on-site investigation, what was important to us was to determine the point of entry and where it landed in the apartment, itself, and to see visually the building where it could have come from. Now, what else should have been done, I couldn't say. I told you the investigation was led by the investigating judge.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see 1D3047. It's a Google view. And perhaps we should leave one of these maps on. Can we get back one of those street plans on one half of the screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On this Google view, can we -- can you identify Miroslava Krleze Street and Hamdije Kapidzica Street, formerly known as Nehru Street?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I could. Just a moment, because this is an aerial view.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If you could also use the school as a landmark, and you can see the bus terminal.

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it now. Should I mark something?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, if the electronic pen is on, please mark the building in Miroslava Krleze Street and the building in Hamdije Kapidzica Street, the two buildings in question.

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this moment, I can only mark the streets. I would not like to mark the buildings because this is an aerial view. What I am marking now is Miroslava Krleze Street [marks], and what I'm marking now is Hamdije Kapidzica Street [marks], as shown on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that both these buildings in Hamdije Kapidzica Street are facing south-west, not south-east? That is, if you drew a perpendicular line onto this building, it would go from south to west?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: South-east, south-west. I did not make these markings south-east or south-west. This photograph is not oriented to the north, so, no, I wouldn't say it is south-east, south-west.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This map is properly oriented. The north is up and the south is down, and we can even see a white meridian going across Dobrinja, I think. This is properly oriented, according to all cartographic rules, and this building is facing south-west, not south-east. Could I ask you to draw a perpendicular line to one of these buildings?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Across my present markings or on the side? I'll do it across all this. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That would be north; right? Do you see the marking in the right angle, where it says "North," what looks like a clock with hands?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can now see that the building is oriented south-west.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the report says "south-east"?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The report contains no orientation at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you just draw a perpendicular line to the building, a line that goes through the building at 90 degrees?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just drew a vertical line through the building. Now I can only draw a perpendicular line to the building, like this [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And that's the south-west. You can now see that the building is facing south-west?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to all of this, the building is oriented south-west, this side that's closer to me, the apartment where the incident happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that between this building in Miroslava Krleze Street and this building, part of the building is hidden from view by the buildings that are perpendicular to Miroslava Krleze Street?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see some buildings that form an L with the building where the incident happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you put your witness number, your initials, and the date. And then we can save the whole screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In order to understand better, can you up-load on the right side of this image Exhibit D970? Oh, we'll lose it. On the right side as well?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Could you put your pseudonym and date of today, which is already February 1st, on the left picture, on the left side.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] KDZ477; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D972, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: During this pause, could I just check if Mr. Karadzic intends to tender the witness's report and the photo file? Because if he doesn't intend to tender them, then I can do so in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Which was 10397. Mr. Karadzic, can you answer the question whether you intend to tender that report?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, by all means. It is very important for it to be in evidence. It would also be good if we could see the photographs in colour, the originals, so that we can see what things are, actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We need to admit it under seal, Mr. Gaynor?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll put it -- we'll mark it for identification, pending translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Which is Exhibit D973, then.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI D973, Your Honours, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: We've had a look for better colour versions of those photographs. We haven't found them, but I believe we can obtain them, so I'll endeavour to do that and submit them to the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That being the case, this will be replaced with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have the first page of the official report again, and then you will decide whether it is going to be broadcast. 09766, that's the 65 ter number. Was there a new number? 09766, that's the 65 ter number, and then page 2. Page 2, please. No, no, the previous page in Serbian, and probably the next one in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The last paragraph here says: "Following the examination of the scene, it has been determined that" so-and-so "was killed at the moment when she was in the bedroom which is located on the south-eastern side of the apartment building, facing the aggressor positions of the Bosnian Serbs based in the neighbourhood of Dobrinja 1 and in the area of the Miroslava Krleze Street. Damage caused by the entering projectile fired from a fire-arm has been found on the left window casement, looking from the window, on the plastic foil that was placed inside the glass at a height of 116 centimetres from the floor," and so on and so forth. We see here that a conclusion was drawn without establishing the angle in relation to the horizontal line; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not my report, so you'll have to ask the person who wrote up the report. How and why this person wrote "south-east," I really have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. While preparing for this trial, you remembered this incident, and you said that you remembered, when you looked at your diary, that you used string to establish the direction of fire; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, that's what I did. However, it is not contained in my report. However, that is what we do when we have such points. On the basis of that and on the basis of this string, I could make this photograph and mark that building with an arrow, the building in Dobrinja 1 from which the bullet had arrived, because I was not saying things just off the cuff. I did it after I used the string.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm a bit puzzled, because your diary does not refer to this string at all, and you said, when preparing for this trial, that it was your diary that jogged your memory. Right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday, I explained what was entered in the diary. So when I go to my office to type up my report on the basis of the measurements entered in the diary, I remembered that I used the string. I did not write everything down in my diary. That diary was used only to jog my memory. However, as soon as I saw that the height was measured and that any measurements were carried out, I realised that a string was used. So my diary is not a detailed report. It is just a reminder for me that I use when typing up my report.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'm afraid that that page remained on the ELMO, and I would actually like to have it admitted, that page, if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The part of his diary?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The page of his diary that pertains to this incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do we have it in e-court, Mr. Gaynor?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: We don't. I think yesterday we were using a photocopy of it. Is that right? I believe that's what Mr. Karadzic submitted, and I don't actually know where that photocopy is, myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it wasn't returned to me from the ELMO, but we'll get it after the break.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's my original diary, but it's no problem, you can use it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. I don't see any problem in admitting that page. Mr. Gaynor?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So we'll mark it for identification, pending translation, that page only.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D974, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now just cast a glance at 1D3047. 1D3047. One will do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see that building again, the one in Hamdije Kapidzica?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you now please mark all the possible directions from which the bullet could have come? Do you agree that it is 180 degrees, that is to say, half a circle?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I disagree. This is the building [indicates], this is the building. I'll put a dot next to it, the building [marks]. But, again, I would like to emphasise that I'm talking now from a particular time distance, so I don't know where the apartment was. So this is the beginning, this is the end [marks]. That's the way it should be. And the bullet came from here, roughly [marks]. I'm going to draw an arrow now, in terms of the approximate direction from which it had come.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How come you know that? How did you rule out 179 degrees and how did you decide for this 1 particular degree from a lower level? Do you assess the distance to be 300 metres, three football fields? Right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stand by the photograph that I took that is an integral part of my photo file, and that is photograph number 10. So the arrow marks that building. Here we have a black-and-white version again. I say, again, that it is certain that I carried out my work quite properly, as best I could, at the request of the investigating judge. On the basis of the measurements I carried out, there could only have been one direction from which the bullet had come. It is not that there could have been several directions, as you had put it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Perhaps the other participants are going to find it hard to understand this, but we have a saying that says "doing things in a make-shift way by using a stick and string." So that's the method that you applied. Can you say from which floor it was fired from the building in Miroslava Krleze?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say that. I said that the arrow marks the building where the fire had come from. I do have to say that when I took this photograph, I took a personal risk at being hit from that very same building. We were not working under normal conditions. We were working under abnormal conditions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us now what the horizontal plane is?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I underline what my report says. It was compiled 16 years ago, and I cannot do it, given the time that has elapsed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: KDZ477, could you place that number again, and could you write down the date as well?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That will be given another number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D975, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D3048, can we have that now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please focus on this trajectory that was marked. This shaded area is the area from which the bullet could have come to the left-hand angle of the apartment in number 10 from the territory held by Republika Srpska, taking account these two buildings through which the shaded area goes. The remaining 179 angles belong to the territory that is under the control of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Do you agree -- do you agree that 5 degrees is the area held by the Army of Republika Srpska, whereas the difference is much bigger compared to the area held by the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see here where it might have come from, and the area is shown very nicely, the building from Miroslava Krleze 10, that it could have gone through these buildings and ultimately arrived at the building where Jasmina Tabakovic was hit. In the previous one, where I marked the previous direction of fire that I marked, it is possible, and it coincides with what I see in the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Although you don't know what the horizontal plane is, and we do know what the vertical plane is, that it goes up 16 centimetres?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stand by that, because the vertical plane was my yard-stick. I used the string to measure this. Unfortunately, we didn't measure how long the room was, but this coincides with this photograph and the possible directions of fire that came at that building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Why didn't you document that, Witness? Why did you decide on this 1 particular degree, and the remaining 179 degrees belong to the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina? How did you decide for this narrow passageway between the buildings? Give us proof. Why, how?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: My objection is that the accused has stated that the remaining 179 degrees belonged to the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. He's twice said that. Now, I don't believe that's in evidence. It appears to be the accused giving evidence. Unless he can show something that's in evidence to support that assertion, he should put that to the witness and ask the witness about it, rather than giving evidence himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. And in addition to that observation, I don't think I follow the meaning of 1 degree, 4 degrees, 5 degrees. Did you, Mr. Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not understand what I was specifically being asked to do. I keep trying to explain that on the basis of the points that I measured, we used a string, and in this way we got a view of the building from which the bullet had been fired. That is to say, I did not establish exactly which window it was, but with an arrow, number 10, I marked the building from where the bullet had arrived. I underline, once again, that we were not working in normal peacetime conditions, so I could not expose myself for too long at that window where the photograph was taken -- from where the photograph was taken. So after using this string, we saw exactly the building where the bullet had come from. I can say that I ran a risk when I took this photograph that is pasted under number 10 in my photo file regarding this incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, please look at this shaded area. Is it correct that the bullet could have come to the fourth floor of this building only through this shaded area?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This perspective, this view we have now, cannot show that. This is a view from above. Now, I don't know how tall the building on Miroslava Krleze Street is, how tall the building in the former Nehru Street is, how tall the buildings are that form an L with the building of the incident where Jasmina Tabakovic is hit. We can only see the shaded area that shows that there is a passage between these residential buildings to the building where the incident happened. What you are asking is impossible to establish with this view.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, with a bullet that ascends, where would it have come from if its source was outside this shaded area? That's what I'm talking about when I say "179 degrees." Where did it come from if it didn't follow this shaded area?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. But it did follow this shaded area, and I established that with the usual procedure with a rope. It came -- the trajectory is marked with this red shaded area. It was shot from one of the lower floors of that building, so it had an ascending trajectory, but it certainly did not come from outside this shaded area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second, Mr. Karadzic. I'm not sure whether the witness has agreed with the place of where that incident took place, which is now marked in blue. Do you agree that that place is the very house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we've cleared that up, that that's the building. The blue is probably the entrance into the Nehru Street number 10, and this beam shaded in red is the area where the bullet had come from. And you'll see the building where this beam begins and follows this trajectory to the building of the incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is the most favourable position of that apartment. If it had been anywhere else, the angle would have been even smaller. Now, if the bullet had come from outside the shaded area, from which position -- from whose positions would it have come from?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know, because I didn't know who held this building, and I don't know it now. Now, looking now, I see that this area that is between Miroslava Krleze and Vojkovici Street -- Vojkovici neighbourhood was under the control of the Serbs, the neighbouring area also, but the airport settlement, I believe, was held by the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Now, who held which building, I don't know, because I didn't walk these lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you are not familiar with these adjacent buildings outside the shaded area? You didn't know who held these buildings?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. For instance, this building in Miroslava Krleze Street, that's the part of Dobrinja 1 that belonged to the Army of Republika Srpska. Whether they also crossed to the other side across this wide street, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where's the separation line here?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. It's possible that the separation line, and I'm talking now about something that was 16 years ago, it's possible that this wide street between Miroslava Krleze Street and this parallel building on the other side was the separation line. I don't know what the name of that wide street is. I believe it's Vahida Maglajlic Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It is. Can you draw that separation line? The marker is off.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The pen needs to be turned on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, according to what I heard from other people, and I didn't go into these streets myself, this should be the separation line [marks], and perhaps the whole length. I don't want to ruin this shaded bit. Now, how far it stretched, I see Dobrinja 4 here, where I lived. I know it was held by the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you extend that line? It went all the way to Trapari, the village houses?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm drawing the whole length now across the houses in the neighbourhood where I lived during the war [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you now see that you could only get to the Serbian side through the shaded area?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, which does not rule out that it came from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I agree it doesn't rule out. You did not rule it out, in fact, but it doesn't rule out the remaining 189 [as interpreted] degrees.

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I did not deal with the horizontal plane in my report, but I did draw that string, and it pointed to that building in Miroslava Krleze Street where this beam of shaded lines begins. And I stand by the work that was done at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's finish with this bit, Witness. Do you agree that 1 degree to the left and 1 degree to the right from this shaded beam are the positions of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and all the remaining degrees outside?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you, I don't know the exact positions. I didn't deal with that at the time. I was always accompanied by one of the colleagues who said where the location was, and you probably have other witnesses who could confirm who was occupying each of these buildings if that's relevant to this Court. I'm unable to say exactly now. I believe that's the separation line, but, again, that's from the stories I heard before or after. I did not go there, because it was dangerous. And I'm not qualified to tell you now who was in those buildings, whether these people occupied them all the time or came occasionally. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you put your number and date, please?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll admit this with the caveat that all the markings done by this witness is only the extended confrontation line, while all the others are prepared by the Defence. Yes, that will be given the next exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that will be Exhibit D976.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, is it the case that all these buildings were occupied, inhabited, from both sides, or were they vacant?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the war, all these buildings were inhabited by civilians. This is a civilian neighbourhood. Now, during the war, which of them were vacant, evacuated, or destroyed, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You came to perform an on-site investigation in a place where people were living. You said you were in fear for your life. You came to do an on-site investigation, and you said you were aware where the separation line was. How come you don't know whether people lived all around you? I am putting it to you that all these buildings were inhabited throughout the war.

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I meant the buildings on the separation line, itself. As for Dobrinja and the place where I did this on-site investigation, this whole central area was inhabited by civilians. Of course, people had nowhere to go. They were forced to live there, sometimes several families per apartment, because they were looking for safety, like everyone else. And all those places that were exposed to fire were poorly frequented, and people were wary of going in, tried to keep under cover. That's how we behaved everywhere around the city. Areas that were exposed to all sorts of fire were dangerous, and people tried to cross as fast as possible or under cover. People were trying to make due, under the circumstances, and had to live there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said the apartment was dark and the blinds were down. Doesn't that mean that the shooter could not see the victim and was not shooting at the victim?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Objection on two counts. Number 1, this has been asked and answered. Number 2, this witness cannot tell whether the shooter could see something, or had night vision, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Agreed, yes, it calls for the witness's speculation. Move on to your next question, Mr. Karadzic. We are sitting for normal hours today, so the first break will be at 20 past 10.00, in five minutes' time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Then we'll move to another incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You were involved in the investigation of an incident that happened on the 22nd January 1994 in Alipasino Polje; correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, briefly, what happened there?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that 22nd January 1994, mortar shells fell on Klara Cetkin and Cetinjska Streets. On that occasion, six children were killed. That is written in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us in what sequence those shells fell, and can you mark it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D02152 in e-court. Perhaps we can zoom in on Alipasino Polje. That's the central area of the map, these two "8"s formed by the buildings. The central area, please, only.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you now be in a position to mark the place of the incident and the sequence of the shells?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That happened in stage C of Alipasino Polje. This map is significantly worse than the one I had before, when I was giving my statement. I can put a circle around the intersection of Klara Cetkin and Cetinjska Street, where this happened. Now, the sequence of the shells, I can't tell you, because I didn't watch them fall. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is very broad. Can you mark the place -- the places -- the exact places where the shells landed?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you, again, it's difficult on this map. I'll just put two dots -- no, it's not good again. It fell on the street, itself, to the left of this dot [marks], and another shell fell again on the street to the left of this dot. It's difficult to mark on this map. We would need to zoom in a lot to see the exact place which would be then consistent with the photo file.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What about a third shell?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't work on the third shell, and that's written in my report, because there were no casualties from the third shell. These first two shells took away six young lives.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was the calibre?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm looking now in my diary. I cannot tell you off the cuff. It says: "Mortar shell, 120 millimetres," and I would like to see my report to see what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you have a copy?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I think it would be best if this is not broadcast, because it contains --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do we not have a public version, Mr. Gaynor?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Well, this was admitted not through this witness, but through a prior witness, as a public exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you like to save this marking or you'd like to do it later on again?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, before we save this, I should like the witness to mark the azimuth, the direction of fire, as he established it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Without my report, I cannot tell you who established the direction of fire. I believe there were ballistic experts present. In this investigation, they established the direction of fire, but I know it came from the west. And I can put an arrow to mark the approximate direction [marks]. The exact direction was established by the ballistic experts. Shall I mark that direction?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do that. We'll come back to it. Put the date and "KDZ477."

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know what was the interval between the first and the second and the third shell?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says around 1315, two mortar shells fell. It doesn't say anything else. I believe the interval was very small.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What about a third?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the third shell. I told you I didn't work on it. As far as this incident is concerned, my job was to photo document what happened. I had ballistics experts on the team who worked also on the third shell. In fact, they used traces from the third shell to be able to write in their report what kind of projectile it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you now put a circle around these two buildings of student hostels, and the "Oslobodjenje" building, but make it separate circles marked with "1" and "2."

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see these two buildings of the student hostel?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, these are the buildings of the student hostel [indicates], and to the left, to the west, this building, the large red one, should be the "Oslobodjenje" building [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mark it "2."

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Put "1" for the student hostel. Put "2" for "Oslobodjenje."

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, who controlled these three buildings throughout the war?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The student hostel buildings were accessible, the "Oslobodjenje" building, too, although it was more risky, because this area was exposed to fire all the time, this area outside the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you draw the separation line here?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's difficult to do now. I can only guess. I never went there during the war. I can put a circle, and I can confirm that buildings 1 and 2 were under the control of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and I believe that even in certain parts of the student hostel there were students who happened to be there when it all began and who had nowhere to go, couldn't go anywhere, so they were forced to live in those buildings.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We can remove -- is this admitted? Did it receive a number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll keep it -- yes, now my microphone is activated. We'll keep it as it is, Exhibit D977. We'll take a break now for 20 minutes and resume at quarter to 11.00, when you will have about three-quarters of an hour to conclude your cross-examination, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was mistaken, Mr. Karadzic. You have an hour and three-quarters of an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have in e-court 65 ter 09390C, sections 9 and 10. This will hopefully be of help to you to find your bearings with regard to the separation line. Can we please just separate sections 9 and 10, if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This is sheet 7. Shall we go to sheets 9 and 10, two pages further.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe this is number 9, but we need both number 9 and number 10 at the same time. Can we please go back to the previous image, where all sections are represented, and just zoom in on 9 and 10. However, can we also have number 1, and that will enable us to enlarge number 9 and number 10. Excellent, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, is this of any help, Mr. Witness, for you to find your bearings?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can see all the three sections of Alipasino Polje, A, B, C, and also the incident site of 24th January.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in one of the reports from your side, it is said that the shells came from the west, slightly towards north?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I recall, members of the team were ballistics experts as well who prepared their report, and I believe it is said in the report that it came from the west or slightly towards the north. However, this can be found in this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you now please mark the incident site and 261 bearing, because that is what has been established, that the bearing is 261?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that's what the report says, then it's 261. So now I am marking Cetinjska Street. It's a bit awkward to do that on the screen. [Marks]. What I have marked is a place that should be in front of the building. Now, that's the place. And the second site is on Klara Cetkin Street, which is to the right, a little bit more left on the driveway.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you make a green circle encompassing both these points?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Excellent. So these are the incident sites. Can you now draw a line towards the west?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that UNPROFOR reached a slightly different conclusion with regard to the bearing?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Since we have to call another document, can you please mark, with the number 1, the place where the shell landed, and number 2, west?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a much -- small map. It would be much easier for me if you could enlarge section C, i.e., to enlarge the intersection of Cetinjska and Klara Cetkin Streets, and that would make things easier for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At the moment, this should suffice, so could you please just make the marking and put the date and the number?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this please be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D978, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So this is the first page of my report, where it reads that two mortar shells of 120 calibre fell on Klara Cetkin and number 3 on Cetinjska Street, respectively. My findings can be found in the next page of my report. This page contains only the basic details.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have the next page in the Serbian language.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please explain what is stated here?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a poor copy. It identifies the place where the shells landed, blood traces. I don't see what is written underneath. I believe it says "parts of clothing and the sledge, and a fragment of a 120-millimetre shell," and I suppose that it says that it has been put in custody with the Crime Investigation Department.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Have we already admitted this report into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we go into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now please have 09951, 65 ter, page 8. I believe this document has not been admitted yet. If we go to page 8, one cannot identify anything on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you say here that you retrieved one tail-fin, and that the other is missing; that you investigated both shells that fell within a short period between them and 100 metres apart. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They fell within the radius of 50 to 100 metres, because that's an intersection of these two streets which join together at this point. One shell fell in front of the building -- residential building number 4 on Klara Cetkin Street and the other one in front of number 3 on Cetinjska Street, so the area where they fell is about 100 metres. I said that I managed to recover one tail-fin, and I think it has been recorded in my photo file, whereas the other one we could not find during the investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How did it happen that in the CSB report it is stated that one shell was 120 millimetres, whereas the remaining two were 82 millimetres?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Part of the team that investigated this incident were ballistic experts who, on the basis of the evidence and clues collected on the ground, were able to produce a report, and this is probably what they wrote in it. I said that two mortar shells exploded, which resulted in the death of six children, and that those shells were of 120-millimetre calibre. Since I only managed to find one tail-fin of a 120-millimetre shell, in the brief description is written what is not the official finding of the expert analysis. The official report is prepared by the ballistic experts after they had analysed the traces. So the fact is that I found only one 120-millimetre tail-fin, and probably as a result of the subsequent analysis carried out by the ballistic expert, it was established that there were two 82-millimetre mines and one 120-millimetre shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm what is written here: "At the same time, there were one or two personnel from UNPROFOR who carried out the same kind of investigation as we did"?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, after such a long time, I really cannot remember. If that's what the report says about their presence, then they were there, but at the moment I cannot remember who attended the incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you have any explanation whatsoever, because you said in your report that the second tail-fin had disappeared? How can you explain that? How can a tail-fin disappear?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The incident took place at 1315, and according to the official documents, it says at what time we arrived at the scene. So during that period, intervening period, it was not possible to secure the scene, itself. That was true, because when we arrived, we did not find any bodies. We only had body parts, the sled, and the remaining fragments of the shell that were collected in the close proximity of the point of impact. How it happened that this tail-fin disappeared, whether somebody took it after the explosion, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I am waiting for the interpretation to be finished. Do you know what conclusions were reached by the UN UNPROFOR team, whose presence you have confirmed here? What did they conclude after their investigation?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had never had an opportunity to look either at the ballistic expert report, or the UNPROFOR report, or the records made by the investigating judge, or the police station Novi Grad. My job was to compile my own report, to prepare my set of documents, and forward it, through my boss, to other organs in charge.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now briefly have document D964, which was admitted through KDZ450. And I'm in the hands of the Chamber as regards the decision whether to broadcast it or not. It's D964.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please focus on the last paragraph. ZK objected to the UNPROFOR statement relating to the massacre on the Alipasino Polje, to which General Soubirou responded that they were not able, on the basis of the traces of the shell, to determine the exact position from where they were fired?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a Muslim document, and it is addressed to the Security Administration?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that was a Muslim one. That was the Bosnian side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, the Bosnian side included Serbs as well. This was the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: But there is no mention specifically of Muslims. There were other ethnicities there as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: There were more Muslims than Serbs and Croats put together. It's already in evidence. Did you pay any attention to the third shell that fell on the building on Rade Koncara Street?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A minute ago, I already said that it was technically impossible for me to make photographs because I didn't have any films. There was a prior agreement for photo files to be made only when some major incidents were involved, which, according to the decision of either the investigating judge or the inspectors in charge, implied that only those shells that caused serious injuries or deaths would be photographed. Since this particular shell did not cause this kind of damage, I did not process this shell. This does not mean, though, that the rest of the team did not carry out their expert work, regardless of the lack of photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Your job was also to collect evidence. Now, concerning the third shell that fell on the soft surface, did you find its tail-fin?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I did not process the explosion site of the third shell. That was done by the ballistic experts who were part of the team. And I think that in that particular instance, the ballistic experts were the ones who processed the third explosion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Just for the sake of exchanging information, Witness, none of the members of the team dealt with the third shell. Is it correct that it fell on a soft surface?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my report, I say that once again, I have not processed that third shell. If you can show the report of the ballistics experts, in their report, their comprehensive report, they had to deal with all three explosions or only the two that we worked on together. If the third one is not there, then nobody had dealt with it. I repeat, once again, that ballistics experts belonged to the same department as I did. However, I was a crime technician and they were ballistics experts. One of these two experts for a while was my superior as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We are now going to move on to the incident in Safeta Hadzica Street. There are two of them. One is at number 102 and the other one is at number 52; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would need the date to jog my memory, and then I could look it up in my diary too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The 26th of May, 1995; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I found it. The 26th of May, 1995, that is a case that I dealt with. It was called the shelling of the neighbourhood of Pavle Goranin in the Street of Safeta Hadzica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, the distinguished Mr. Gaynor showed a photograph of a shell that fell in that garden by number 102. I don't need to call it up. You do remember the photograph, don't you, with the onions that were planted there where the shell allegedly fell?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember the photograph. I took it. It is one of the 10 projectiles, cannon projectiles, that had fallen on the ground there. It was in the immediate vicinity of the police station where I was. Behind the place where the explosion took place, there is a wall of the open garages belonging to that police station. The red roof, as far as I can remember, covering these garages is the roof of the police station. In this photograph, we see an arrow that marks the place where the explosion happened. Yesterday, I was asked whether that marks the direction from which the projectile had come. My answer was that that was not the direction from where the projectile had come. It was only subsequently, when the photo file was being compiled, an arrow was put there to show the place where the explosion happened. So it could have been made in any way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you for this exhaustive answer, but I would just like to underline another thing. Yesterday, we heard from you, for the first time, and we are grateful to you for that, that that was a police station and that there were garages of that police station there. Did you take part in the investigation at Safeta Hadzica 52, in relation to the incident that took place there?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The building in Safeta Hadzica number 52 is part of the investigation of the overall incident that we are discussing now, so there was no separate investigation. Investigating Judge Eterovic was in charge of it. There were inspectors from the State Security Service -- from the Public Security Service were there.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please don't mention any names. This document was admitted as a public one, I think. 65 ter 09784, 09784. I don't know what the status of that document is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: My understanding is that it was admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then it shouldn't be broadcast or we should move into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you would like to name the protected witness, we need to go into private session. But if you do not, we can stay in public session without broadcasting this document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then the second option, not to have it broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please cast a glance at this official report. It has to do with this incident; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. This is an official report that was compiled on the 1st of June, 1995, and it has to do with the incident that occurred on the 26th of May, 1995, between 10.45 and 10 past 11.00. The members of the team are referred to here, the ones who carried out the expertise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The report says that there were different shells there and that one of them was of great destructive power. You're actually referring to a modified air-bomb; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, so it is Safeta Hadzica number 52.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have 1D2198. Could we have that in e-court. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a Google image. Can I now ask you to mark the location of the incident and a few other locations? Can you mark the location of the incident, the building that was hit in this incident?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were 10 cannonballs and one air-bomb in this incident. You asked me about that photograph a moment ago, where it fell on the earth. The air-bomb fell on the right-hand side, on the extreme right, say 150, 200 metres. That was the entire area that had been shelled and ultimately hit by an air-bomb. I can put a circle around the buildings that were hit during that incident and the area around the buildings. It wasn't only the buildings that were hit, but the area around them as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's focus on the air-bomb, the building that was hit by the air-bomb.

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm putting a circle around the building that was hit by an air-bomb. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it on the left side or the right side in relation to Majdanska Street?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From my point of view, it's on the left side. On the right-hand side of that building is Majdanska Street that goes further down to the Bulevar of Mese Selimovica, or, rather, the municipality of Novi Grad.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you now put number 1 there by that building that had been hit?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you kindly to put a circle around the police station. Mark that with number 2.

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Number 3, that is the school. Could you mark the school with number 3?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The transformer station, please, number 4.

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The municipality of Novi Grad, could you mark that, please, number 5?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please put a circle around the Geodesy Institute, number 6?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Then the TV building, 7?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. To the right of this, number 7, what is that on the other side of the river? Is it Astra or Unioninvest, or what is that building?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's Gras. It's the garage of Gras.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you mark that, too, the garage of Gras?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Number 8; right? Now, you think that between this police station and the building that was hit, there's about 150 metres; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot say with any precision. The area can be calculated, but it's the length of Safeta Hadzica Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you place "KDZ477" and the date? Perhaps we'll have to call up other documents if you don't have them in hard copy; your statements, I mean.

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that's admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D979, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, on the 11th of March, 1997, and on the 24th of April, 2006, you said that on the 26th of May, you were in the police station when an air-bomb flew over -- or, rather, this projectile, when it flew over the police station. During your proofing when you testified in the Milosevic case, General Milosevic case, in January 2007, you changed that. You said it wasn't the 26th of May. You said it was, rather, on the 28th of August, 1995, or, rather, on the 28th of July, I think -- no, or the 28th of June, actually. Can you explain this to us? While preparing for this testimony, how did you manage to remember, 12 years later, that that was wrong and that you wrongly believed, over the course of 12 years, that it was a particular date, and then all of a sudden, during proofing, you remembered that it was a different date?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: During both incidents that occurred in Safeta Hadzica 52, and I don't know the exact date when the Kuwaiti Infirmary was hit also by an air-bomb, I was at the police station on duty as the duty crime technician. I was gave that explanation yesterday when I was questioned by the Prosecutor. To this day, dates don't mean anything to me. However, there is one thing that remained imprinted in my memory, and that is the flight of this projectile. I was in the police station. The window was facing westward; that is to say, in this part which faces the municipality of Novi Grad. I was in an office that faces the west. Now, during which one of these two incidents I saw, well, I cannot say that after all this time now, I cannot say exactly what was in which statement. I'm telling you the dates didn't really matter to me, but what I remember full well is that one of these two incidents, Safeta Hadzica 52 or when the explosion over there happened to the south of this building of Safeta Hadzica 52, on one of these two occasions I did see the projectile fly over. It wasn't in both cases, just one of them. Now, which one it was, I cannot remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In 1997 and in 2006, you said that it was on the 26th of May. So in two statements that were closer to the actual incident, that's what you said. And then while you were preparing for the third time to testify in General Milosevic's case, you changed that. Do I need to call this statement of yours up or do you still remember what you said?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to underline the time distance, once again, and the statements that I gave in the period that you're referring to now.
