Then I think that perhaps the first variant would be more plausible quite simply because there is this time distance. That was the first statement that I gave. That was closer to the 26th of May. And I don't know when the other explosion took place, I don't know the exact date, but I'm trying to say now that we shouldn't really waste any time over this. I don't know the exact time, but I will accept that as I stated it in the first statement, let that be it, because I think that less time had elapsed from the incident until the time when I made my statement on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In that statement, you say that you were very close to the location of the incident when it took place, and then you indicated on the photograph the roof of the police station where you were when the bomb exploded. The bomb came over the police station from the west; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It came from that direction. The windows were facing west. I cannot say that it came over the police station exactly, because I was looking at it and it was a bit further to the south in relation to the room that I was in. So it's not that it flew over, it's not that I had to raise my head. I saw it. I saw it on my left as I was standing on the -- at the window.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have this in e-court, this Google one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please, could you now mark what it was that you saw, the direction that this shell came from? You have what we used a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm going to use a dot to mark the wing of the station where I was [marks]. The projectile flew this way [marks], so that would be it, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you go to the building that it hit?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the building [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The usual thing, "KDZ477" and the date, please.

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted, this photograph?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, as Exhibit D980.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said you had seen the shell fly?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for a second or two. I don't know how long it was, but I saw it fly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said it made a lot of noise, a racket, like somebody revving up an engine?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was just trying to describe what I heard, and that was approximately that sound.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was it the sound of rocket engines?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was there any smoke?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In your statement of 24 April 2006, you say precisely: "I conducted investigations on places of impact of modified air-bombs. I saw such one bomb fly before it hit. It was the 26th of May, 1995. The bomb flew over the police station before it hit the Street of Safet Hadzic. It had small, stubby wings --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speaker slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this the correct description?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it looked like to me at that moment, those couple of seconds that I had to watch it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In your opinion, rocket engines were on at the time, they were propelling the rocket?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was flying, so they must have been working.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I was advised that we have lost the markings done by the witness just now, which is D980. Do you like the witness to do the markings again which shows the direction of projectile?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He remembers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please look at e-court and do the same thing you did before to mark the direction. You can mark the station, the direction.

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm now marking the building that was hit by that air-bomb [marks]. Now I'm marking the station [marks], and now I'm marking the direction of the projectile [marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And your pseudonym and the date, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was the height -- the altitude at which the shell was flying?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly. Whether it was at the altitude of the high-rise or above the high-rise, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did it fly in a straight line or was it a parabolic line?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was a straight line. Whether it was falling down or not, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So it flew by the police station, not over the police station?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I was in the window, and I was watching it fly on my left side. It was not directly above me; it was to my left. And looking from that window, it would be the west side.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this photograph be admitted or does it already have a number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, it was admitted as Exhibit D980.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You worked on many more incidents, as we can see from your statement. I would, therefore, like to look at incident involving the Elektroprenos bus. Was it on the 18th of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, 18 August 1995, the intersection of the ninth transversal and Safeta Hadzica Street. Object, the public utility company Elektroprenos bus.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see photographs showing that type of bus to see what kind of bus it was that was hit. Can we see 1D3038.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You've seen those pictures of buses?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: These are our photographs. This is the kind of bus. Was that bus one of these three types?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot really talk about the type of bus. I don't think we need this, because there are photographs of that bus, original photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We'll be very grateful if you can provide them, please.

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I made a whole photo documentation. Do we have that photo in electronic form?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope the Prosecution can assist. Otherwise, we can put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: We have photographs in hard copy, and I'll just get them right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: These are -- these are hard-copy print-outs which were provided to us by the witness at the weekend, and they are -- he can explain their relationship to the photo file, but they were used -- they were the same ones as were used to create the photo file.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence would like to receive those photographs, and we also kindly ask that a copy be made for the witness to mark some things we need. But there is no photo of the bus in this documentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd like to point out that these photographs were, in fact, notified to the Defence on Sunday, and the Defence has, in fact, inspected these photographs. I'm going to see if there are any photographs of the bus. One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With all due respect, we would like to have these photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: My apologies. I handed over the wrong batch of photographs. This is the batch here. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. These four photographs could be of assistance, but we really need to ask the witness to make some drawings on them. Can we make photocopies of these photographs so the witness can mark them?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please look, in e-court, at the third bus at the bottom. It's just the same as the one on your photograph; do you agree?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bus that I see could be. But without the photograph, I can't claim it's exactly the same type. I need a photograph. I made a photo file, and I believe, just with the other incidents, it should be in electronic form with a caption underneath.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need photographs for this testimony, but we also need it for our own expertise, for our own expert report, so we have to have them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This red bus is the original bus, and the photograph was made recently from the original negative that is kept with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. And if you look at this other photograph, the bus that is blue or turquoise in colour, you could see it's from the same manufacturer, but the difference between them is that the blue bus has a door in the middle and the red one, the original one, doesn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you show, here on the bus, where the shell impacted?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We see damage on the bus here, where the body was twisted, and then we can see the same on another photograph - it's marked with number 1 - and this deviated part of the bodywork is also clearly visible. And that's what it says in my report, the bus was hit just above the window.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: From which direction did the shell come from in relation to the bus?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bus was hit on the right side while crossing the intersection between Deveta Transverzala and Safeta Hadzica Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a photograph from inside?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this was taken from the inside of the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see that this exit hole is just next to the frame of the window?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This damage was created when the projectile exploded. I don't know which kind of projectile it was. I'm not a ballistics man; I just photographed the damage. And it's true that it hit the upper part of the window. I don't know which window in sequence it is. We could see it on one of the other photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We'll need to get photocopies to mark them. But do you agree that this inside damage is just next to the frame of the window?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The whole frame of the window was twisted, as well as the roof.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see again the previous photograph to see the outside damage.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here, you can see clearly that the frame was hit in full, and we saw the damage it created on the inside. We can put both photographs on the ELMO at the same time. Now you can see the inside and the outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, regarding the horizontal plane, do you agree that the entry impact is a bit more forward than the exit hole? Look at it carefully.

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 1 is marking the whole damage created. It just marks the point of impact. Under what angle and how it entered, it's difficult to see on these photographs. They just show specific damage created by the impact of the projectile. Now, what angle, that's difficult to say, all the more so because the photograph was taken at a certain angle in both cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Based on the traces, based on this distance from the frame of both the entry and exit holes, can you make any conclusions about the direction of the projectile vertically and horizontally?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't. I can only say the bus was hit on the right side, above the window on the bodywork, but I cannot be more specific than that, based on this damage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that determining the direction is decisive in determining the origin of fire?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but we can get that direction if we know the bus was hit on its right side.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll now look at that intersection. I would like these photographs to be admitted. But we would really need photocopies of these photographs after the break so that the witness can mark these things, although they are pretty clearly visible. Maybe both these photographs can be admitted under one number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D981, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Somebody did make a determination. Was it you or somebody else from the team that determined the calibre and type of weapon involved?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It couldn't have been me. It must have been one of the ballistics experts. But if you want me to say anything at all about it, I need the documents of this investigation, my whole report, the whole photo file, the statements of ballistics experts, the findings of other members of the team, if you want any comment from me.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask that the witness be given all that?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: According to the witness's amalgamated statement, his report should be 65 ter 09884. If that's to be called up, it should not be broadcast. And there is another report which is compiled by an inspector from the CSB, and that is 65 ter 09885. Neither of those have yet been admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gaynor. Just a second. I noted that this document was briefly broadcast. We may need to redact it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether I was mistaken or not. I'll leave it in the hands of the Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, will this be of assistance?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is my report, where it says what case it is, and it says that it's shelling, and the intersection where it happened, and what actually happened. The bus of Elektroprenos, a public company, was hit, and then there is a description that follows. And on the second page is this same report continued and my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The former Street of Ive Andrica in this case is called the 9th Transversal; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and it continues from the Street of Ive Andrica from the north and then moves down south to the intersection with Safeta Hadzica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please have a look at this. The projectile hit the metal plate, et cetera, while the bus was moving towards the Olympic Village. Is the type of weapon identified anywhere and the calibre? It seems to me that somewhere in these reports it says that it was a PAT, an anti-aircraft gun. Right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my report, it says "projectile," exactly. I did not say what type at all. Quite simply, it is because I could not establish, on the basis of the damage on the bus, what weapon was involved. I left that to the ballistics experts. The vehicle was moving when it was hit. It was moving towards the Olympic Village, and I can read it: "While the vehicle was moving from Alipasino Polje towards the Olympic Village, the projectile hit the metal plate above the first large window next to the front door." So this is an exact reference where the bus was hit, the first large window next to the front door.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we go through this further and see whether the report contains anything more specific? Does anyone know what type of weapon was used? Paragraph 112, you say the bus was hit on the right-hand side with an anti-aircraft bullet, you say. So what would the weapon be, a machine-gun, because it's not an explosive charge?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The report that I wrote up is more important, the one I wrote after visiting the scene. I'm reading the names of the people who were on the team. I'm reading it from my diary. I don't know if it would be right for me to read the names. I can say it was a member of the KDZ. I'm not going to give the name of that person. So at the time, he was in charge of dealing with the traces and sending everything for further expert evaluation to see what projectile was involved. Now, whether they gave an official report as to what projectile was involved in this incident, I don't know, but I didn't want to say anything specific. That's why I wrote "projectile." What kind of projectile it was, perhaps I said it later in my statement, but perhaps it is not the result of my having read an official objective report, but perhaps I just heard somebody say it. If we are specifically interested in that, we'd have to read the official report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please ask for them to leaf through this report further? But in 112, you say that it was an anti-aircraft bullet, so that would be a machine-gun, wouldn't it? And the last sentence says. And that's what you said when you gave your statement of the 15th of November, 1995, and you repeated that when you testified in General Milosevic's case on the 31st of January, 2006, transcript reference 328, that's the ERN number: [In English] "The shot could only come from the VRS-held territory." [Interpretation] So you are drawing an unequivocal conclusion here that the shot could only come from VRS-held territory. That is why it is so important for us to see whether it is direct or indirect fire, and we need to test this conclusion of yours that purports not to leave any doubt. Please ask for a paper copy of the report, or let's leaf through this further.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. President, I can provide the witness with paper copies of his report and of the report compiled by the CSB, if it would assist the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have in e-court 65 ter 10179, 10179; P147 in General Milosevic's case. It's a map. Can we have a hard copy too, just one.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: The two reports that the witness has just been provided with are, as I said earlier, 65 ter 09884 - that's his report - and the CSB report is 09885. And if either of those are to be broadcast, they should -- or to be brought up, they should not be broadcast, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No need to have it broadcast. We have a map here now that pertains to Grbavica, and that's not what we are asking for. 65 ter -- I mean, it's paragraph 113. It should mark the place where the bus was hit. It's not this map that we see here now. Can we then have 09390C, and then section 10. Maybe that's it, yes. Actually, give us section 10. 65 ter 09390C, and then section 10. Can the left-hand side be zoomed in. Further. Actually, the lower part of the left-hand side. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you now mark the location of the incident for us, Safeta Hadzica and the 9th Transversal, the location of the incident?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm going to mark the intersection of Ive Andrica and Safeta Hadzica, where the bus passed before it was hit [marks], and in this circle we should see the place where the bus was actually hit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was the bus already there? Had it already reached the intersection, or did this happen before or after the intersection?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not an eye-witness. So this intersection is a dangerous one. That's what we called it. It was visible from the neighbourhood of Nedzarici, and from time to time, different types of fire were reaching it coming from different kinds of weaponry. There was no protection there at the time, and I'm sure that the bus was moving faster than it would when it was moving through areas where there were many buildings. You can look at the statement of the driver, himself, where the bus actually was, if he does make a reference to that in his own statement. I was not an eye-witness. As for the bus, itself, and for taking its photograph, I did that when it stopped in Dobrinja, together with the investigation team.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Which route was the bus supposed to take? Was it supposed to continue along Ive Andrica or Safeta Hadzica and then Ante Babica? Can you mark the route it took to Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm going to explain how it moved by using short arrows [marks]. So this is the route of the bus before it stopped. So it moved down Ive Andrica Street, it crossed the intersection with Safeta Hadzica, and then it went further on, not through Mojmilo, but around it, and then it went down to this narrow area that was protected visually at the time. There were containers that provided visual protection, and then the bus could be sheltered that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mark where the containers were?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't finished yet. As for the intersection between Ive Andrica and Safeta Hadzica, there were garbage containers there, and I think that that can be seen in my photo file. However, they did not provide enough visual protection. Now, I don't know how many of them were there and what visual protection they could provide to the bus, in view of the Nedzarici neighbourhood. As far as I can remember, when I went to on-site investigations, garbage containers were there all along the road. However, there was no visual protection by Dobrinja 5. Certainly, there was more than at the intersection of Ive Andrica and Safeta Hadzica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: First of all, you found glass there on the actual site, and you believe that that is the point of impact, although you say that vehicles were crossing along that -- over that shattered glass. Where was the glass and where was the impact?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The very intersection of Safeta Hadzica and Ive Andrica, somewhere around there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please put number 1 and number 2 there, that is to say, the location of the incident, and, to the west, the containers?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. I put a circle around the intersection where it happened. And this short line that marks number 2, that's where the containers were lined, and that would be much clearer if we looked at the photograph. You could understand immediately what kind of visual cover it provides relative to the height of the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you say these shards of glass were all over the intersection, exactly on the intersection, and the front of the bus was on the intersection?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That should be it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell the Trial Chamber: From the separation line, how tall are these buildings across the separation line? What neighbourhood is that to the north-west?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the north-west is stage 2 of Alipasino Polje, the Square of ZAVNOBiH.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mark it?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Apologies to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, number 3, how tall are these buildings?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm marking number 3 to denote stage B of Alipasino Polje [marks]. Ten days before coming here, I made new photographs, and I turned them over to the Prosecution, photographs showing this neighbourhood. Those are several-storey buildings around the periphery of the neighbourhood, whereas buildings on the square are five, six storeys tall. To the south-west of number 2 is Mojmilo neighbourhood. It's an Olympic project, also a residential/civilian area. The buildings are several storeys high. I don't know exactly how tall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you also put a circle around Mojmilo?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Number 4 there, please.

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, these buildings towards the separation line, what are those neighbourhoods? Is that stage A?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is stage B [marks]. It says on the map "Mojmilo." I don't need to mark it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: To the west of stage B, what's there?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Saraj Polje, also a civilian neighbourhood adjacent to Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Put a circle around that. Does it have a name?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vojnicko Naselje, "Soldiers' Settlement."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this the student hostel to the north of the Soldiers' Settlement?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Should I put a circle around there?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mark the Soldiers' Settlement with "5" and student hostel with "6."

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What's this building that remains standing alone next to Mojmilo?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This should be the health centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Put a circle.

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How tall are these buildings in number 5?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Several storeys high.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you put "7" on the health centre?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that Nedzarici is a Serbian neighbourhood, with detached houses, with no tall buildings in it, that the tallest is the Home for Abandoned Children, two storeys high?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that those were private houses. They still stand today. They had two or, maximum, three floors, including the loft. And as for the layout of the terrain, which you cannot see on the map, from the place of the incident marked with "2," there's a downhill slope. On this map, you see Mojmilo Hill, so naturally the whole street, Safeta Hadzica, goes downhill towards this transversal line, Ante Babica Street. You can see that on the map, and Nedzarici is at the foot of this slope.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, do we again find here a very narrow area on the Serbian side that could have potentially been the origin of fire, a very small, narrow space between buildings, so it would practically take a miracle for a bullet to find its way through? Can you now draw a line to the possible origin of fire on the Serbian side?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will not agree with what you just said, because this is not an extremely narrow space. This is a very large field in Safeta Hadzica Street, a very large space from which you could fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now change the pen, use red, and draw a line between the health centre and the northern building.

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You can shade it, please.

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, what's the direction vertically? Did it go -- how did the projectile go, horizontally or from -- or downwards or upwards?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Upwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But if we look at the photographs, we see that the exit hole on the inside shows a downward line?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Okay. We'll come back to that. Now, tell us all, please: We have here a possibility of 360 degrees, so if the bus was just before a turn, 180 degrees, you opted for these 5, 6 degrees, how did you rule out the remaining 180 degrees? Which method did you use to exclude the possibility that the origin of fire was elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first of all, the bus was hit on its right side, and I said that in my report. I don't want to repeat it. I photographed the bus in Dobrinja, and it indicates that the bus was coming from down-town towards Dobrinja. If it had been on its way down-town, it would have been hit on its left side. In addition to my report, which is typed up and photographs attached to it, there are reports of other members of the team, and there are statements of several witnesses who were on the bus, itself, and who can confirm that the bus was moving and where it was moving, so it's indisputable that the bus was moving from down-town towards Dobrinja in the direction I indicated on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, we now need perfectly reliable information about the type of weapon. Is it a weapon that produces direct or indirect fire? And we need angles on a horizontal and the vertical plane to be able to make determinations. Do you have these angles?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does anybody have them?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says in my report that the bomb squad from the CSB Sarajevo extracted pieces of the projectile. They were analysed, and that analysis helps determine the type of weapon used in this incident. There are other documents that speak about the type of weapon that fired on this intersection not only in this incident, but also in the past, and there is also documentation of all the shelters that were put up to reduce the risk. And I knew that this intersection was risky, because I lived close by, and that it was open to fire from Nedzarici. That's why the shelters were placed as they were placed. They provided cover from Nedzarici, not from Mojmilo and not from other areas, because it was common knowledge that there was constant fire from Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Why weren't there any shelters put up facing Mojmilo and other areas?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because no incident was recorded where fire came from those places.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's see if it was ever established, and how, that this fire came from the Serbian side. Is there anything -- any document in the report about the angle of descent of this projectile, and where can we find it?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't help you there. There was a whole team working on that investigation. It was led by the man under number 1. I was part of that team. And in addition to the two of us, there was also an employee of the Counter-Sabotage Unit from the Security Services Centre, the Novi Grad station. You have to ask that man, because we sent him all the documents in this file, and he was supposed to send them on to the investigating judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please put "KDZ477" and the date.

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]

utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.text: The wire factory?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you know where Unis and Igman were?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The entire block of buildings just behind the TV building is what used to be the industrial area before the war. We all -- we referred to the whole area as the wire factory, but I don't know which part you mean precisely. I know that somewhere to the east, the Astra chemical factory was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please place a date and your signature.

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We'll use a particular software application to show you another view of this area. Do you know what brigade was deployed in this area, the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina brigade.

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see it clearly, but I think it was the 101st Mountain or Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Has this been admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: D986. And, Mr. Karadzic, you will have five minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have Sanction on. Yes, we see the 101st. You can remove the signs. We have the 155th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this the area of responsibility of the 101st Brigade?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you anything about the AORs. I know the 101st was there. As for the neighbourhoods where I conducted my investigations, I can tell you that these were civilian neighbourhoods, inhabited by civilians, both Alipasino Polje and Pavle Goranin. You are now showing me certain front-lines, where I was not, and I don't know where the areas of responsibility of the respective brigades were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's have a look at the headquarters and various staffs of the 101st Brigade. Did you know that there were command posts in the area? Did you know that there were command posts?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a police member. I was not a member of the 101st Mountain Brigade so as to know where their command posts were, as designated here. I can only tell you that I see the former Viktor Bubanj Barracks. I don't know whether you meant that. I am really not familiar with this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do we have the artillery and howitzer positions? Yes, we do. Do you see the tank?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see there is a tank. Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you see that in the TV building, there was a company command?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As anyone else in the courtroom, I can only read to you what the map says.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we zoom in on the company command and the TV building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I don't see any point of pursuing this line of questions further, given the witness's answer that he doesn't know about these positions, Mr. Karadzic. But, by the way, has this been provided to the Prosecution, this programme?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, we provided that. However, it can be joined with other material. We are still awaiting further documents. There is nothing here that is not based on certain documents. And here you can see, for example, what document is referred to when we designated the company command post in this particular location.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I understand we do have the programme. We don't have the underlying material upon which this is based or any indication as to methodology.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Please conclude your cross-examination very soon, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I'll be -- I'd be happy to. Could we please have the 111th Brigade. We need to zoom out for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.text: Can you see that the 111th Brigade went all the way up to the Muslim part of Vogosca? You can see their positions and headquarters there. Were you aware of it?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We won't be tendering anything as yet. I just wanted to show you what the things looked like. Let's have a look at the military-purpose industry facilities, and that will be my last topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you see the facilities I mentioned? The entire industrial area was geared towards production for the war. Were you familiar with that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you know that a transformer station you marked provided electricity to these ammunition and weapons factories behind the TV building?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't aware of that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Witness. This concludes my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karadzic. Mr. Gaynor, before you re-examine the witness, the Chamber has a question for the witness. Judge Baird.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Witness, in testifying about your investigations in respect of the incident in Nehru Street, you stated that you did not deal with the horizontal plane in your report, you dealt with the vertical plane. Do you recollect this?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It had to do with the incident when Jasmina Tabakovic was killed. In that case, an investigating judge was with me on the team, and he was in charge of the investigation. I was only determining the height, in terms of the location where the damage was, and later on we brought these points together and we determined the line. However, that line was not measured in the room, itself. However, on the basis of these points, we were able to tell from which position the bullet had come.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: I thank you. But Dr. Karadzic asked you, at page 12, lines 16 to 18, words to this effect: "All these things being done -- being what they are, the horizontal plane and the horizontal inclination are decisive in determining where the bullet came from?" Now, we didn't quite follow the answer you gave. Are you in a position to tell us, Witness, would the horizontal plane and the horizontal inclination be decisive in determining where the bullet came from?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Horizontal measures were not included in the report. However, on the basis of the vertical ones that we did do, we determined only the direction from which the bullet had arrived. However, this was not included in the report, not my report or the reports of my other colleagues who were on the scene.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: So am I correct in assuming that you would not be able to comment on that question by Dr. Karadzic, whether the horizontal plane and the horizontal inclination -- whether they are decisive in determining where the bullet came from?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this moment from this position, I am not in a position to do so on the basis of the horizontal one. But on the basis of the vertical one and the photographs I have from that period, I was in a position to confirm from which position the projectile had come.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gaynor, do you have re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I do, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Witness, I'd like to stay on the same incident that His Honour has just been asking you about. And prior to discussing that incident, I want to ask you a few questions about the methodology of investigating sniping incidents, specifically. Now, when you use the string that you describe, could you explain exactly where you put the two ends of the string?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The investigation team always consisted of a minimum of two members. It was necessary to establish the way in which the bullet had entered a particular facility. When assessing the damage that was caused by the bullet, we were following the trajectory and looking for traces in the said facility. Only when we would find the second point that could be linked up to the first one, in terms of the damage caused by the bullet, it was only then that we could stretch the string. We called that "viziranje." So that string or that twiglet that was used to show where the bullet went, that could only be done if we had two or more points. If we had just one point, if we had just a single piece of damage on a window, for instance, it would not be possible to do that, and it would not be possible to establish the origin of the gun-shot. Then we would have to talk about a wide range of possibilities, in terms of where that bullet could have come from.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Before we get to the specifics of this particular incident: Is it the case, yes or no, that sometimes an optical device is used, as well as a string, in the investigation of sniping incidents?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nowadays, that is a perfectly normal thing. But at the time when I investigated these incidents, our technical abilities were very limited. We did not have the resources that are used today when carrying out these investigations.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Turning to the specific incident, the killing of Jasmina Tabakovic, you say in your statement that the bullet entered through a plastic sheet. And we can bring up the photographs, if you want, but could you describe to Their Honours approximately how big the penetration hole would have been?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, since these are plastic sheets that were used instead of glass, because glass had been shattered during the shelling, damage on that plastic sheet could have been 1 centimetre, at a maximum. It's been a long time now, but I think that the photo file shows this, 1 centimetre, maximum, unless the plastic sheet was completely torn. But I think that the circle was up to 1 centimetre in diametre.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Turning now to the impact point of the bullet on the wall, approximately how big was that impact point?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since it's a hard surface, I think - it's not that I think; I'm sure - the damage would have to be bigger, because when the wall is hit, then mortar crumbles, and also the concrete that was behind the wardrobe that the bullet had hit.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could I bring up the exhibit, not to be broadcast, D973. I'd like to go to one of the photographs that you took of this incident which shows the size of one of the penetration points, and I'd like to see photo number 7. That should be the 10th page of this. If we could just hone in on the lower photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you describe which of the points this is?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The caption shows that the damage was caused by the bullet hitting the wardrobe, and that is marked with the number 6. It's a terrible photocopy, but I think that there is a dark area above the number 6 that actually shows the damage done by the bullet.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, could you explain for Their Honours the process of taking a string and taking it from this point to the point of penetration in the plastic sheeting? Is that what you did, or could you just explain exactly what you did?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we entered the room where the incident occurred, the room was visually observed. What was observed was that on the plastic sheet, there was damage caused by the bullet. As we further investigated in the room, we realised that the wardrobe was damaged as well. Before the wardrobe was moved, and that was done subsequently, this measurement was taken. Only when the wardrobe was removed, and it was against the wall, not exactly against the wall, there were a few centimetres in between, we saw that there was damage on the other side of the wardrobe and in the wall, itself. As far as I can remember, and that is contained in my report, the bullet stopped in the wall, and that's where we actually found it. So all of these points, starting from the penetration point on the plastic sheet, and then hitting the wardrobe, and the other side of the wardrobe, and then the wall, all of that is along a single line; how the bullet went through that room, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And just tell us how you came to the conclusion that the bullet had come from Dobrinja on the basis of the observation of those points. How exactly did you come to that conclusion? From Dobrinja 1, I should specify.

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of all of these points, we established that these were fresh traces. It's only when we removed the wardrobe and when we saw the damage on the wall, itself, that is, the final destination of the bullet, and we also saw the penetration point on the plastic sheet, that was the original point of damage. So when we brought those two together, and when we looked at the string stretched between the two, we saw the building that we had discussed. So after the visual protection was removed - I'm referring to the blinds that were there - that building showed up. A photograph was rapidly taken, of that location, that is. Because of safety reasons, we could not establish the exact area, although this was quite sufficient to determine the roof of the building, or a window on the building, or some other location. However, in agreement with the other members of the team, it was deemed sufficient to take a photograph of the building from which the bullet had come into this room.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you. And now I just want to deal with a second point dealing with this incident. Mr. Karadzic drew your attention to the fact that the trajectory of the bullet was upwards. So the initial point of entry was at 116 centimetres, you measured, and the point of impact on the wall was 132 centimetres, which means it travelled a vertical distance of 16 centimetres while it was in the room. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall that. It is true that all these measurements are not in my report. That is to say, from the moment when the bullet went through the plastic sheet until it stopped in the wall, it was moving upwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. Your report is actually quite specific on this. Now, Witness, could you tell us how long, approximately, the room was from the point of impact -- from the point of entry to the point of impact, to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up to five metres, maximum.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Very well. Now, Witness, I won't take you or the Court through this in great detail, but if I were to say to you, and I'll invite the Defence to agree this, if the length of the room was five metres and the bullet travelled a vertical distance of 16 centimetres, then the angle of the bullet's trajectory was 1.83 degrees, that was the upward movement of the bullet, Witness, I won't necessarily ask you to agree with that, but do you have any reason to disagree with it?

utterances.speaker: KDZ477 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the angle was a very small one. Now, how big it actually was, I cannot say exactly. However, in terms of the height at where the bullet entered, and if we take into account how big the room was, say five metres, the angle was quite small. It went upward, and the angle was small.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. No further questions. Thank you, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I? May I just put one question to the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you could tell us what the question is in advance.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in view of the housing situation in our part of the world, there were never bedrooms that were five metres long in our part of the world. A living-room could be five metres long, but not a bedroom. A bedroom would contain one or two beds, and that would be it. And it's very important to see how big this angle is, to see that it did go upwards. And if there were to be a difference of only 2 degrees, the picture obtained is quite different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's not for you to give evidence, Mr. Karadzic. Mr. Gaynor, what --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, I quite agree, Mr. President. And, simply so the Defence might be able to agree something on this, if the room was as short as three metres, the angle would have been 3.05 degrees. If it had been four metres long, the angle would have been 2.29 degrees. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you have any comment, Mr. Witness, as to the size of the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've already said that the maximum was up to five metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Witness. That concludes your evidence, and on behalf of the Tribunal and the Bench, I thank you very much for your coming to The Hague to give it. So now you are free to go, and please have a safe journey back home. But before that, please wait until we draw the curtain.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we open up the curtains. Given the time, it would be impractical to call the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: There are three matters to deal with before we adjourn for today. Who will be leading evidence of Mr. Hogan?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: This will be Mr. Hayden.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I looked at his 92 ter statement briefly, which is a document of only two pages to which are attached two schedules, which seem to be a kind of result of his investigation as regards the F and G incidents, and I take it he's going to produce several exhibits. So I wonder whether he needs to be classified as a 92 ter witness. As a matter of fact, there will be no difference between leading him viva voce in its entirety and introducing him as a Rule 92 ter witness. Yes, anybody could answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The only thing is that in the statement, he may refer and give already details in relation to certain exhibits. But you are correct, Your Honour, it will not make a big difference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So he can introduce that exhibit as a live witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So that witness will be lead live, viva voce.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. And the next issue is related to the request of Mr. Karadzic to have Dr. Subotic during his evidence. We considered the matter, and, in conclusion, we do not consider it necessary or appropriate for Mr. Karadzic to have the assistance of someone with Dr. Subotic's expertise during that testimony of Mr. Hogan, given the nature of his anticipated evidence. We note that an intended assistant to Mr. Karadzic in relation to this witness, Mr. Hogan, is not as an expert, and that Mr. Karadzic has other options available, such as requesting OLAD to bring Mr. Sladojevic back from his trip early so that he can provide the accused with the support that he normally receives. Should Mr. Karadzic wish to replace Mr. Sladojevic or one of his other Defence team members with Dr. Subotic, that is a matter for Mr. Karadzic to discuss with OLAD. Therefore, we will, on an exceptional basis, permit the presence of Dr. Subotic in the courtroom for Mr. Hogan's evidence, but on the understanding that this creates no additional financial implications for the Tribunal's Registry. For the next matter, we need to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, the next issue relates to Dr. Zecevic. I take it you received the information which is contained in the memorandum of service.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we did. I'd also note that Mr. Gaynor is present, who has also dealt directly with that, so we have -- and Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff -- are in the best position at this point to answer the Court's inquiries.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: At this moment, we find it helpful to hear from the Prosecution, what you consider should happen next, in light of the development; in particular, the information in the memorandum of service. Yes, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, the two issues that are very distinct is, first, the health issue that he raises. I think that can be easily overcome by granting the video conference request that we have made. Although the medical documentation is from April last year, people know that back problems are long-lasting, and, therefore, I think that can be overcome by the videolink -- granting a videolink. In relation to the dissatisfaction that he was -- in relation to the fact that he has to testify yet again before this Tribunal, we have tried to explain to him why that is necessary, and that his earlier testimonies cannot replace that entirely, but he did not seem to be open to our remarks on this topic. Therefore, my -- I have a very practical solution, I think, whether that's at all possible. If the President of this Trial Chamber would write to him a personal letter, explaining it to him again why it is necessary that the Trial Chamber hears from him in person, it may be that Mr. Zecevic changes his mind. Otherwise, I see no other option as to enforce the subpoena.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: By writing a letter, do you mean that this Chamber exploring of the possibility of him coming as a Chamber witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: That would probably change his mind, that's correct. But I was actually thinking about explaining to him, in a letter, why it is necessary that the Trial Chamber has to hear from him, and that he has to give testimony again, and why, at this point in time, nobody can actually grant him the requests that -- the conditions that he has imposed. You may remember that he has asked for 180 minutes' testimony altogether, actually allowing him to do that now, already granting it now, and we have tried to explain to him that this is not an option that we have, as the Prosecution, but we would inform the Trial Chamber of his request. But he still seems to maintain that the Prosecution is unwilling to follow his requests, and I think that may be one of the reasons why he is so dissatisfied. And it seems that we cannot reach him with our arguments any longer. That was actually the thinking that I had.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Having heard his submission, that he was minded to come to The Hague, but he would give his evidence only for three hours, why not call him to come over to The Hague instead of hearing him via videolink, given the opposition from the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I only noticed that he again stressed the fact that he can only sit for 20 minutes at a time, and travelling here would definitely include a longer sitting time. That was only my concern about his health issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What did he say? He could sit for 20 minutes and he needs 60 minutes walking or practice exercise?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, that's what he says here in the letter that was attached to the filing, 20 minutes sitting at a time and afterwards a need for a 60 minutes' walk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson, do you have any observation to make on this?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. With respect to the request for a letter, we don't have any objection to that. We note that the Chamber has written letters on our behalf on a few occasions to Mr. Tudjman and even before this Chamber came on, Judge Bonomy wrote a very strong letter to Carl Bildt which encouraged him to meet with us. So it has worked in the past, and if it can work this time, short of other enforcement methods, we don't have any problem with the Chamber doing that if it's minded to do that. With respect to the videolink, we are very strongly opposed to that and we'd prefer that their other options be explored, such as bringing him to The Hague or postponing his testimony until his back is better, because we still have another year of Prosecution witnesses to hear. And this witness, given the importance of his testimony, we really feel that this is a situation where videolink would disadvantage us on a very practical level.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm just putting this hypothetically.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The transcript doesn't say that we are strongly opposed to videolink. Please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We understood that. In case the witness refuses every option, it is still the opinion of the Prosecution that it would be useful to arrest him and bring him to The Hague or to the Liaison Office?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, but Mr. Gaynor spoke to him, actually, recently. Perhaps he can add one issue in relation to the videolink conference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: By all means. But we have to go out of the courtroom very soon. Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. Simply to put the point that he is simultaneously putting forth the position that he does have serious health concerns and that he is willing to travel to The Hague if his demands, as he describes them, are met. So he has not, himself, expressed a great enthusiasm for the concept of a videolink, but that is -- that, to me and to many of us, has seemed to be the logical answer. But he has spoken, himself, about travelling to The Hague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you for that information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: In point of fact, Mr. Gaynor, not only has he spoken about travelling to The Hague, but he tended to play down his illness, didn't he? One formed the impression that it wasn't -- the illness wasn't that important, but isn't that your impression?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Well, it's one of the reasons he puts forth now as to exactly which is the determining reason for his lack of co-operation. To be honest, we haven't been able to fully establish that ourselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Which one.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. We go back to open session. Yes, Mr. Robinson, in the private session or open session?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we are now in open session. Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, just for one second to advise you yesterday we filed simultaneous documents with respect to Venezuela, and we will withdraw our request for a hearing in light of the Trial Chamber's third invitation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. That's done. So we'll hear tomorrow Mr. Rechner's evidence, tomorrow at 9.00. So the hearing is now adjourned for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 2nd day of February, 2011, at 9.00 a.m.
